title: Finite algebras over a local henselization have finite-type strict local models
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, let $R_0$ be a finite-type $D$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak q\subset R_0$ be maximal with separably closed residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-separably-closed]. Let $H=((R_0)_{\mathfrak q})^h$ be the local henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], let $\widehat H$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $C$ be a commutative $H$-algebra finite as an $H$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose $\widehat H\otimes_H C$ is a nonzero local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $C$ is a Noetherian strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. There exist a finite-type $R_0$-algebra $F$, a maximal ideal $\mathfrak z\subset F$ over $\mathfrak q$, and a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z=\operatorname{Spec}F$ supported at $\mathfrak z$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with an isomorphism of $R_0$-algebras $C\cong\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Z,\bar z}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. In particular $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is finite type and the image of $\mathfrak z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ is the specified closed point $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Expose V, proof 2.2.7 (finite algebra descended from the local henselization); strict-local form in Expose XVII, final paragraph 6.5. Algebraic identification: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05WP, lemma-quasi-finite-henselization; locality and henselianity: Tag 04GH, lemma-finite-over-henselian. The completed tensor being local selects the unique factor.

proof.text: Put $A=(R_0)_{\mathfrak q}$ and $k=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. First identify the residue field of $H$ with $k$, including its structural embedding. The field $k$ is henselian: its maximal ideal is zero, so the idempotent-lifting condition is the identity map for every finite $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] applied to the local residue map $A\to k$ gives a local map $H\to k$. On residue fields the composite $k\to\kappa(H)\to k$ is the identity. The second map is an injective field homomorphism whose image already contains all of $k$, hence both maps are inverse isomorphisms. Thus $H$ is henselian with separably closed residue field $k$.

source.place: Tags 04GN (lemma-henselization), 04GQ (definition-henselization); elementary universal-property argument for the residue identification.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] $R_0$ is Noetherian, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] so is $A$. Apply [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] to $A$, its henselization $H$, and the separable closure $k/k$. There is only the trivial finite separable subextension. Its finite local etale lift is $H$ itself, by the uniqueness clause, so this identifies $H$ with the algebraic strict henselization of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3), applied to $Y=U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ at its closed point with the residue closure $k$, this pointed-etale colimit is canonically the triples colimit of $(A,\mathfrak m_A,k)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], the ring called $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ in [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. Consequently [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] makes $H$ Noetherian. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega_0$ of $k$ and the corresponding geometric point $\bar q$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. Its separable residue closure inside $\Omega_0$ is $k$. The affine comparison [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], with affine open the whole scheme, identifies $H$ with $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}R_0,\bar q}$, as an $R_0$-algebra with the prescribed residue map.

By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] $H\to\widehat H$ is faithfully flat. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to the $H$-module $C$ gives an injection $C\to\widehat H\otimes_H C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], write $C\cong\prod_{i=1}^r C_i$ with each $C_i$ a nonzero henselian local finite $H$-algebra, local over $H$. The hypothesis that the completed tensor is nonzero rules out $C=0$ and thus $r=0$. If $r\geq2$, the element $(1,0,\ldots,0)$ gives an idempotent of $C$ different from zero and one, and its image under the injection is still such an idempotent. A local ring has no such element: $e(1-e)=0$ and one of $e,1-e$ is a unit, since their sum is one. This contradicts the assumed locality of the completed tensor. Hence $r=1$, so $C$ is henselian local and $H\to C$ is local.

Write $\mathfrak n$ for the maximal ideal of $C$ and $L=C/\mathfrak n$. The residue-field clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] gives a finite extension $L/k$. By [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-sep-closed], $L$ is separably closed, so $C$ is strictly henselian. A finite set of $H$-module generators of $C$ also generates it as an $H$-algebra, since every element is an $H$-linear combination of them. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes it finitely presented over $H$.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] with $R=R_0$, prime $\mathfrak q$, and separable closure $k/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3), applied to $Y=U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ and the geometric point $\bar q$ of Step 2 (whose separable residue closure is $k$), this triples colimit is canonically $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}R_0,\bar q}$, compatibly with the maps from each $S$; with Step 2 this presents the ring $H$ of Step 2, as an $R_0$-algebra, as a filtered colimit of etale $R_0$-algebras $S$ pointed by primes $\mathfrak p$ over $\mathfrak q$ and $k$-embeddings $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to k$. Work with a small representative diagram of these finite-presentation algebras and their point data. Apply [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent] to this filtered diagram and the finitely presented $H$-algebra $C$. We obtain one such $(S,\mathfrak p)$, a finitely presented $S$-algebra $F$, and an $H$-algebra isomorphism $H\otimes_S F\cong C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], $S$ is finitely presented over $R_0$, hence finite type. Finite presentations give finite algebra generating sets, so the union of generators of $S/R_0$ and $F/S$ generates $F/R_0$. In particular $F$ is finite type over $R_0$.

source.place: Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different), Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), part (1), and Tag 00U1 (definition-etale); ILO Expose V 2.2.7 finite-presentation descent.

proof.text: The embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to k$ in the selected triple is a $k$-embedding, so it identifies $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $k$; $S/\mathfrak p$ also equals $k$, since it contains the image of $R_0/\mathfrak q=k$. Let $\bar p:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_0\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ be this residue point. The etale map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ is ind-etale by the constant diagram in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], using finite presentation from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization]. By [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance], its map of strict localizations identifies $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}S,\bar p}$ with $H$, compatibly with the chosen colimit leg $S\to H$: by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](4) with $V=W=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $w$ the identity, the functorial map $h$ carries the leg of $(\operatorname{Spec}S,\bar p)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}R_0,\bar q}$ to the structural map of $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}S,\bar p}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3) (Step 5) that leg is the triples leg $S\to H$. Let $H_p=(S_{\mathfrak p})^h$. The elementary residue argument of Step 1 gives $\kappa(H_p)=k$. Apply [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] again with the trivial separable closure $k/k$, and [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] to $\operatorname{Spec}S$. It identifies $H_p$ with this same strict local ring. All identifications are over $S$. Thus the map $S\to H$ is an ordinary henselization at $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tags 04GW, 0BSL, 04HX; invariance under an etale neighbourhood, as in algebra.tex Tag 05WR (lemma-quasi-finite-strict-henselization), etale case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] to $S$ and $\mathfrak p$, using the $S$-algebra identification of Step 6. It says precisely that $S\to H$ is ind-etale. The equality $C\cong H\otimes_S F$ of Step 5 identifies $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ with the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. Hence the base-change assertion of [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] applies to this morphism and identifies its strict localizations at every geometric point, compatibly with the map to $\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), property (2), and Tag 04GV (lemma-henselization-different); Tag 0GIP (lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite), filtered-colimit argument.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak z\subset F$ be the preimage of $\mathfrak n$ under $F\to C$. It is prime, and its preimage in $R_0$ is $\mathfrak q$, since $H\to C$ and $A\to H$ are local. The injection $F/\mathfrak z\hookrightarrow L$ is an injection of $k$-algebras. Because $L/k$ is finite (Step 4), $F/\mathfrak z$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. For each nonzero $b$ in this domain, multiplication by $b$ is an injective linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space, hence surjective; in particular $b$ has an inverse. Therefore $F/\mathfrak z$ is a field and $\mathfrak z$ is maximal. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $L$. The residue map $C\to L\to\Omega$ gives a closed geometric point $\bar t$ of $\operatorname{Spec}C$, whose image $\bar z$ in $Z=\operatorname{Spec}F$ is supported at $\mathfrak z$.

source.place: Elementary contraction and finite-dimensional-domain argument; the finite extension L/k was proved in Step 4.

proof.text: The identity $C\to C$ is a henselization of the henselian local ring $C$, by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Since $L$ is separably closed, apply [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] to $C$ and the trivial separable closure $L/L$: its only finite local etale lift is $C$ itself. Thus $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}C,\bar t}\cong C$, using [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] for the geometric formulation. Combine this with the strict-localization isomorphism in Step 7 at $\bar t$. It gives $C\cong\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Z,\bar z}$ over $F$, hence over $R_0$. Finally $F$ is finite type over $D$: adjoining the finitely many generators of $R_0/D$ and those of $F/R_0$ generates $F/D$. Thus $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is finite type, with the required specified closed image $\mathfrak q$.
